welcome.title: Welcome
welcome.content: Welcome to the Workspaces page. One view of the workspaces across all of your projects, and the fastest way to review work from your agents. Share feedback anytime via the navbar icon.

commandBar.title: Command Bar
commandBar.content: The command bar is your central hub for navigation. Open it with CMD+K to search and access every action available in a workspace.

contextBar.title: Context Bar
contextBar.content: The context bar lets you switch between panes quickly. Drag it wherever works best for you.

sidebar.title: Workspace Sidebar
sidebar.content: See the status of all your workspaces at a glance. Notifications highlight which ones need attention. Archive merged workspaces to keep your sidebar clean.

multiRepo.title: Multi-Repo Support
multiRepo.content: Add multiple repos to a single workspace. Reference code from one repo while working in another, or implement changes across several repos at once.

sessions.title: Multiple Sessions
sessions.content: Create multiple agent conversation sessions within a single workspace, including sessions with different agents. This helps you work around conversation limits or spin up review agents in separate threads.

preview.title: Preview Changes
preview.content: Preview your work in a built-in browser without switching contexts. Test across desktop, mobile, and custom viewport sizes.

diffs.title: Diffs and Comments
diffs.content: The redesigned diffs panel includes a file tree of your changes. Comment directly on diffs to give feedback to the agent, and view GitHub comments when your workspace is linked to a PR.

classicUi.title: Return to Classic UI
classicUi.content: Click the exit icon on the left side of the navbar to return to the classic kanban board. To disable the new UI entirely, update the "Enable Workspaces Beta" option under "Beta Features" in settings.

intro.title: Welcome
intro.content: Welcome to Prepcook. Use the help sections in this panel to learn how things work, then create your first issue. You can re-open this help dialog or give feedback anytime from the navbar.

welcome.title: Projects
welcome.content: The project page is where you manage issues. You can view your issues as a kanban board, or as a list, and filter by status, tag, assignee and more.

issues.title: Issues
issues.content: Each issue represents a feature or problem to solve. Issues have statuses, priorities, assignees, tags, relationships, comments, sub-issues and more.

workspaces.title: Workspaces
workspaces.content: To start working on an issue, create a workspace. A single issue can have multiple workspaces. Issues describe the work to be done, workspaces are where the work happens.

chef.title: Chef mode
chef.description: Prepcook does the prep. You approve plans and move the cards.

prep.title: Prep mode
prep.description: Prepcook drives tickets through the gates.

onboarding.title: Set up Prepcook
onboarding.lead: A prep cook does the prep so the chef can cook. Pick the coding agent that does the work, the editor you open its worktrees in, and the sound that tells you a session has finished. Three steps, about a minute.

agent.name: Coding agent
agent.question: Which coding agent does the work?
agent.helper: Every stage starts from this agent. You can give a stage its own agent or variant later in Settings → Agents.

editor.name: Editor
editor.question: Where do you open code?
editor.helper: “Open in editor” opens a session's worktree in this editor. You can change it later in Settings → General.

sound.name: Sound
sound.question: What should a finished session sound like?
sound.helper: Prepcook plays this when a session finishes running. Pick one to hear it.

onboarding.permissionsNote: Prepcook runs coding agents with --dangerously-skip-permissions / --yolo by default. Always review what agents are doing.

journey.title: What happens to a bug here
journey.helper: Each stage is a column on the board. A card moves left to right; Prepcook works the middle, you hold the ends.

todo.name: To Do
todo.description: You import a ticket or make a card, and send it to Plan.

plan.name: Plan
plan.description: Reproduces the bug against a local build and writes an RCA. Waits for your approval.

execute.name: Execute
execute.description: The smallest fix for the mechanism the RCA isolated, with regression tests.

review.name: Review
review.description: An independent review in a fresh worktree; request-changes goes back as a fix round.

shipped.name: Shipped
shipped.description: Pushes the branch and opens the pull request, reproduction attached. Once it merges, you clean the card up.

cleanUp.name: Clean up
cleanUp.description: Worktrees archived; the RCA stays in Knowledge.

noTracker.title: No tracker? That's fine.
noTracker.description: Without one, every card is made on the board and the card is the only record. Connect Jira, GitHub Issues or PagerDuty later in Settings → Ticketing.
